name: LockedUSB Charge Only Adapter
one_line: USB adapter that physically disconnects the data lines so a connected device can only charge, blocking juice-jacking attacks.
why_notable: A defensive anti-juice-jacking data blocker rather than an attack tool, but it directly demonstrates/mitigates the O.MG-Cable-style USB data-line attack surface.

name: Vidar attiny85 based BadUSB
one_line: Miniature ATtiny85 USB stick emulating a keyboard and firing a pre-programmed payload on plug-in; firmware user-modifiable.
why_notable: Minimal cheap ATtiny85 BadUSB from a different maker than the tracked Digispark/CH552 boards.

name: Evil Crow Cable
one_line: ATtiny85 BadUSB cable with data lines enabled, emulating a keyboard to run pre-programmed payloads. No Wi-Fi.
why_notable: Same brand as the tracked Evil Crow Cable Wind but genuinely different silicon - ATtiny85 with no ESP32-S3 or Wi-Fi, at half the price.

name: EvilDuck
one_line: Open-source HID keystroke-injection board: the SD variant runs an Arduino Micro (ATmega32U4) executing DuckyScript from SD, the S3 variant an ESP32-S3 with browser-based remote payload control.
why_notable: 355 stars, last commit 2026-06-06. Different MCU targets from the tracked Rubber Ducky/Digispark/pico-ducky boards.

name: USBvalve
one_line: Firmware for a Raspberry Pi Pico that sits inline on a USB port and shows on a screen whether a newly connected device is reading from or writing to the host, to flag BadUSB behaviour before trusting an unknown drive.
why_notable: 1344 stars, last commit 2026-08-19. Defensive counterpart to the BadUSB devices already tracked.

name: Multifunction Network Box
one_line: Linux-based network appliance with an LCD status display that logs and selectively blocks traffic across up to 16 GbE ports during an engagement. Price range $1,500-$3,000 by model (Model 100 / Model 1000).
why_notable: A purpose-built covert network-implant/traffic-control box, more capable than the passive taps already tracked, with no equivalent in the DB.

name: PiKVM v4 Plus
one_line: Hardware KVM-over-IP remote access unit with a built-in 3/4/5G modem, marketed by the seller as an undetectable remote-access tool for red-team engagements (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Cellular-connected out-of-band remote access hardware, a distinct implant category from the USB/network-tap tools already tracked.

name: Gigabit Ethernet Tap
one_line: USB-powered passive single-port 10/100/1000BASE-T network tap with PoE pass-through, in a small metal case.
why_notable: Only Gigabit-capable Ethernet tap seen on the site; the taps already tracked (Throwing Star, Plunder Bug) are 10/100 only.

name: 10/100 FastE Switch Tap
one_line: USB-powered 5-port 10/100 Ethernet switch with port mirroring (port 1 to port 5) and PoE pass-through, used as a network tap.
why_notable: A switch-based network tap, mechanically distinct from the passive inline taps already tracked.

name: Firewalla
one_line: Inline network appliance (quad-core ARM, 512MB RAM) between router and LAN, passively monitoring connected devices for threats, filtering content and offering VPN and ad-blocking through a mobile app.
why_notable: Consumer defensive appliance rather than a testing tool - weakest fit in this batch. Recommend dropping.

name: Glytch GPS Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: GPS add-on module for the WiFi Pineapple Pager that geotags captured networks/clients for wardriving (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Adds location-tagging to WiFi Pineapple Pager wardriving sessions, a real functional addition rather than a passive accessory.

name: LittlePcap Network Tap
one_line: Inline dual-gigabit-Ethernet tap writing captured traffic as PCAP files directly to an attached USB drive; USB-C powered, roughly 16s boot.
why_notable: Captures to its own USB drive, unlike the tracked Throwing Star and Plunder Bug which need a separate capture host.

name: Glytch Ethernet Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Wired Ethernet add-on for the WiFi Pineapple Pager enabling LAN-based payload deployment in addition to its WiFi radios (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Turns the WiFi-only Pineapple Pager into a wired network implant as well, similar in role to a LAN Turtle.

name: Netgotchi Pro
one_line: Battery-powered ESP8266 + OLED variant of Negotchi with the same scanning, honeypot and alarm functions, configurable by onboard buttons or a phone web portal.
why_notable: Portable version of the same maker's scanner line.

name: Negotchi - network security scanner
one_line: ESP8266 + OLED board that periodically scans the local Wi-Fi network for hosts and vulnerabilities and runs a honeypot service, sounding an on-screen alarm if the honeypot is touched.
why_notable: Standalone intrusion-detection gadget - a different category from the tracked wardriving and deauth boards.

name: Glytch Ethernet Mod for Pager
one_line: 3D-printed add-on using an RTL8152B USB-to-Ethernet chip to give the WiFi Pineapple Pager a wired RJ45 port.
why_notable: Stock USB-Ethernet controller with no security-specific circuitry - closer to the generic-adapter exclusion than the other two Glytch mods. Recommend dropping.
